$MU $SNDK $SKHY Fair question, and the honest answer is: plenty, starting with this industry.

Micron itself, 2018. At the peak it traded at roughly 4 to 5x forward earnings, with gross margin at a filed 61% in Q4 of fiscal 2018, and the stock still lost about half into 2019 as earnings collapsed. ZIM, 2021 to 2022: near 1 to 2x peak earnings, enormous dividends paid out in cash, and still down roughly 80% from the peak when container rates normalized. US homebuilders in 2005: roughly 6 to 8x peak earnings, after which earnings went negative and the stocks fell 70% and more. Dry bulk shipping in 2007: low multiples on peak charter rates, then declines of 90% and more.

The common thread is not the multiple. It is that the earnings were spot-priced. When the spot price turned, the denominator vanished, and the low multiple turned out to be the market pricing that evaporation in advance. That base rate is exactly why memory trades at 2x and not 12x today.

Where this cycle differs is confined to the contracted share: multi-year agreements with minimum pricing, and 12.9B dollars of contract liabilities on Micron's balance sheet at fiscal 2026 year end per its 10-K, cash collected in advance. No name in the precedent set had that construction. The uncontracted share of memory earnings carries precisely the risk those names did, and contracts themselves can still be amended by mutual agreement, which is the channel to watch. en_summary: (Reposted by @JonkooTrades) $SPCX - Morgan Stanley concludes a single Starship launch with Starlink V3 pays back variable cost in about 19 weeks of operating profit, less than half the time for SpaceX's AI compute business. Keeps Overweight rating and $300 price target, more than double current. Full payload 50 Tbps gross, 2.5 Tbps salable. V3 satellites 10x downlink of V2 Mini. Starship launch 20-25x bandwidth of Falcon 9. Expects Starship to cut variable launch cost from $1,000/kg in 2026 to $500 by 2030 and $140 by 2040, weekly launches by end 2027. text:
$SPCX - Morgan Stanley works through the economics of a single Starship launch carrying Starlink V3 satellites and concludes that it pays back its variable cost in about 19 weeks of operating profit, less than half the time it estimates for SpaceX's AI compute business. 

It keeps its Overweight rating and $300 price target, more than double the current price per share.

Morgan Stanley puts a full payload at 50 Tbps of gross capacity, of which 2.5 Tbps is salable. 

The step up from the current fleet is large:
- Each V3 satellite has about ten times the downlink capacity of the V2 Mini satellites flown on Falcon 9. 
- One Starship launch adds 20 to 25 times the bandwidth of a Falcon 9 launch, equal to two or three months of Falcon 9 Starlink flights. 
- SpaceX stopped flying Starlink missions on Falcon 9 from Florida in late August, leaving Vandenberg as its only Falcon 9 Starlink pad. 

Morgan Stanley also expects Starship to cut SpaceX's internal variable launch cost from about $1,000 per kilogram in 2026 to about $500 by 2030 and about $140 by 2040, and expects weekly Starship launches by the end of 2027. It notes that Starlink V4 is planned at roughly ten times the capacity of V3 again.

At about $140 the stock is 4% above its $135 offer price, while Morgan Stanley's 2027 and 2028 EPS estimates have risen 80% and 60% since early July. 

It calculates 17.5 times its own 2028 earnings and 11.2 times consensus, both excluding tax benefits, against 16 times for the S&P 500.

text:
博通和谷歌的目前合作关系挺有意思的，我把官方说过的话和市场传的消息放在一起理了一遍。

先说没变的。4月两家签了长期协议，博通继续为谷歌开发和供应未来几代TPU。6月陈福阳说谷歌给的是一笔数额非常大的金额承诺，没给数字。9月他又说，博通计划未来几年每年交付几百亿美元的TPU。

变了的是，博通不再是独家，这是它自己承认的。6月有分析师问到份额，陈福阳说：我们当然想拿下每一个设计，但谷歌需求涨得太快，我们完全预期他们会有多个来源。

另一个来源是联发科。供应链传得很凶，郭明錤说下一代v9和再下一代v10都由联发科独家设计，这周又说谷歌砍了明年100万颗博通做的8i。谷歌和博通都没回应。

但两家公司自己的说法没这么绝对。陈福阳9月说，2028、2029年谷歌的需求，会由"我们今天正在和谷歌一起开发的"后几代TPU来满足。

联发科10月的电话会上，管理层说它的第二代AI芯片2028年一季度量产，市场普遍认为这就是谷歌的v9，公司没有点名。有分析师问，到了这一代，你们会不会成为这家客户的主要供应商。财务长答的是：跟所谓的竞争项目比，对方性能差得很远。这等于承认了v9这一代是有竞争项目的。但目前我猜V9主力应该像外界说的给了联发科。

至于再下一代，也就是市场说的v10，蔡力行说定义还要时间才能定下来。谈到整体竞争时他说得很克制：对手很强，我们会赢下属于我们的那部分，说明当时还没定下来。

9月高盛科技大会上有一段问答很有意思。主持人问：投资者担心谷歌把越来越多的设计收回去自己做，你们的护城河在哪？陈福阳没有正面回答谷歌会不会这么做，讲的全是技术：高速接口、SerDes、多芯片集成、先进封装。然后说过去30年博通一直靠工程能力赢对手，这次也一样，不管对手是同行，还是，用他的原话，"更有意思的是"，客户自己。

把客户算进竞争对手，说明他很清楚谷歌在做什么。

我的理解是，合作的重心换了。核心计算单元谷歌可以自己设计，这部分博通守不住。值钱的地方挪到了怎么把多颗芯片拼成一颗、让它们高速通信，这正好是博通最强的。

这个判断对不对，下一代就是考试。联发科那款是多颗芯片拼的，封装换成了一家美国IDM的工艺，新伙伴、新制程、新封装一起上。联发科说进度正常，良率还在爬。顺利量产，顺利量产，说明这道护城河别人也跨得过去；

出问题，谷歌手里还有博通已经在量产的v8，以及博通正在开发的后续型号。

一句话概括现在的状态：钱还在，独家没了，下一代两家都在做。12月9日博通财报，看管理层怎么回应。

以上是个人思路，不构成投资建议。

zh_summary: 簡單來說：波動率 $VIX 飆升等於彈簧壓縮。波動率快速回落等於彈簧反彈。只有快速反彈才是良好買入訊號。波動率從高位回落的速度很重要，而不僅僅是下跌。單獨的飆升只表明恐懼上升，但沒有說明燃料是否會快速釋放。快速波動率回落迫使集中的Delta回補買入，創造尖銳底部；緩慢下降則將買入分散，沒有彈力。
en_summary: Simply: a vol $VIX spike = spring compresses. FAST vol collapse = spring snaps. Only a FAST snap is a good buy signal. The speed of the vol collapse back from high vol matters, not just that it falls. A spike by itself just tells you fear is rising. It tells you nothing about whether the fuel will be released fast enough to matter. Fast vol collapse forces concentrated Delta buybacks creating sharp bottoms; slow decline spreads buying with no pop.
text:
Simply : a vol $VIX spike = spring compresses. FAST vol collapse = spring snaps. Only a FAST snap is a good buy signal. The speed of the vol collapse back from high vol matters, not just that it falls. A spike by itself just tells you fear is rising. It tells you nothing about whether the fuel will be released fast enough to matter. You're waiting for the release, not the compression.
 
Here's why:
 
Fast vol collapse = forced buying in a burst
• When volatility spikes, traders get caught short "Delta" (they're short stock as a hedge).
• If vol then collapses quickly, all those traders are forced to buy back stock at roughly the same time — a big, concentrated burst of buying.
• That burst is what creates the sharp, meaningful bottom and the strong rebound. 
Slow vol decline = buying gets spread out and wasted
• If vol just grinds lower slowly, the forced Delta buying happens in small trickles over weeks or months.
• Each little bit of buying gets absorbed by sellers. There's no concentrated "wall" of demand.
• The "potential energy" never gets released all at once — it leaks out harmlessly. 
The analogy: Think of it like a compressed spring. A vol spike compresses the spring (builds potential energy). A fast release snaps the market upward. A slow release just lets the spring uncoil gently with no pop.
 
So the sequence that actually matters for a real bottom is:
1. Vol spikes hard (panic, fear, implied vol expands)
2. Vol collapses fast (fear drains quickly)
3. Forced Delta

Watching AI stocks absolutely puke is a reminder about how beautifully timed Anthropic’s IPO was. Now that it’s done, the worse the capital markets get, the better it is for Anthropic.

Post-IPO, $ANT has nearly $250 billion of cash on its balance sheet, a cash flow breakeven (or better) business, and the possibility its main rival may be stuck private, cash-burning, undercapitalized, and incapable of cracking compute-efficiency the way Anthropic has.

At the same time, Anthropic’s suppliers are now staring into a late-2027 compute glut, the supply of which basically can’t be stopped given existing inertial forces. That could leave Anthropic sitting pretty as a renter with spot market exposure - picture Eddie Murphy and Dan Akroyd at the end of Trading Places, standing calmly in the pits taking orders from desperate counterparties.

In fact, Anthropic has every motivation to encourage and FACILITATE a glut.

The worse the capital market environment gets, the better it is for Anthropic’s long-term prospects.
